messages:
Maria: Quick heads-up — starting a compatibility sweep of Dedicated H100 pools tomorrow 2025-06-01 13:00 UTC. Target stack: NVIDIA driver 535.86, CUDA 12.2.0, NCCL r3.4. This is a phased sweep (waves) not a full rollout.
Sean: thanks — what's the wave size and selection criteria?
Maria: Wave-0: 8 reserved hosts (non-prod) in us-west2 for functional smoke. Wave-1: 30 hosts spread across eu-west1/us-west2 (mixed tenants) for latency + throughput smoke. Wave-2: 100 hosts limited to dedicated test pools, then gated for production.
Priya: test matrix? perf, KV cache, nccl allreduce sanity, and driver load/unload stress. Also verifying runtime kernels for fp16 and int8 quant paths.
Devon: schedule noted. How long for each wave?
Maria: Wave-0: 1h window (smoke + rollback sanity). Wave-1: 3h window (increasing load). Wave-2: 6h with canary throttles. If any latency p95 regresses > 20% or error spike >0.5% rollback immediately.
Tanya: add a cost guard — if tokens per minute drop and autoscaler spins up extra dedicated nodes we'll hit overage. Recommend setting temporary cap on burst for the sweep.
Sean: +1 on cap. I'll flip a soft quota: dedicated-burst-cap = 20% for the sweep window.
Priya: Also instrument kernel oops and dmesg into the trace stream. If we see repeated nvidia-mig reset logs or "EID 0x1" NCCL connect timeouts mark severity-1.
Devon: For rollback, what's the precise procedure? We need exact commands for Private and Hosted fallback.
Maria: Rollback playbook (short):

```
# rollback driver on a host (ssh)
sudo systemctl stop redwood-runtime
sudo dpkg -i /opt/nvidia/driver-535.57.deb  # previous known-good
sudo reboot   # prefer controlled reboot via oncall
```

And for Dedicated control plane we have automated rollback via the agent: `redwood-agent rollout cancel --wave $WAVE_ID` which will pin the pool to previous kernel-driver pair and drain new allocations. Link: https://go/redwood/playbooks/driver-rollback
Sean: good. Ops-bot, add rollback snippet to the incident channel if any canary fails.
ops-bot: noted — will post automated alert to #incidents if 2/3 canary hosts fail healthchecks within 15m. :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: Canary job scheduled: job_id=canary-1855-01, start=1855072400, hosts=[h100-usw2-0..7], smoke-suite=v3. Instrumentation: traces=on, perfbench=on.
Tanya: If we need to fallback regionally, what's failover plan? e.g., if eu-west1 shows regressions do we route eu customers to us-west2?
Maria: We prefer model variant routing first: route impacted requests to the compatible cpu fallback or to A100 pools in-region if capacity permits. If not, route by policy to us-west2 with geo-notify. Coordinate with Support for customer comms.
Priya: Important to test NCCL topologies — some hosts use p2p across two switches. We'll run allreduce stress with `nccl-tests` configured for 4 GPUs and variable message sizes (8KB->8MB) to reproduce multi-size patterns. Capture packet drops and nvidia-smi pmon.
Devon: Add kernel parameter check: ensure `iommu=pt` hasn't been toggled on kernels for wave hosts. We saw issues last year when iommu changed.
Maria: noted. Preflight checklist (short):
- confirm quota cap (Sean)
- baseline perf snapshot (Priya)
- canary job scheduled (infra-bot)
- rollback commands pinned in runbook (Maria)
- customer routing policy validated (Product)

Sean: I'll temporarily disable aggressive batching for canaries to avoid masking latency regressions.
Priya: How do we detect subtle memory corruption from kernel-change? Add long-run memtest in wave-1 background and check for UVM faults in dmesg.
Tanya: We'll also enable cost telemetry alerts: if spend rate > forecast + 12% for the hour, auto-pause non-critical dedicated autoscale.
Maria: Good. If we hit anomalies we escalate: Pager to oncall -> infra-sre -> eng-runtime. Use escalation matrix in playbook.
Devon: One more ask — record a short A/B delta: same prompt set on previous driver vs new driver to catch quality/perf regressions in generation (we saw cache invalidation cause weird latency spikes).
Priya: Will run 5k prompt perf corpus, capture p50/p95/p99, token/sec, and failed-generation count.
ops-bot: reminder scheduled: canary start in 24h. I will post a 30m and 5m reminder in this channel.
Maria: Thanks all. Post any blockers here. If wave-0 looks clean we'll proceed to wave-1 after a 30m hold. :rocket:
Sean: 👍
Priya: 👍 running preflight now, will paste baseline outputs 30m before start.
Devon: I'll be on-call for rollback.
Tanya: I'll monitor cost and autoscale.
infra-bot: canary job started (canary-1855-01) — first smoke complete, 0/8 failures, p95 latency delta +3%.
Maria: Great. Keep status updates short in this thread. If anything shows >10% p95 regression or any NCCL connect errors escalate immediately.
infra-bot: wave-0 status @ +18m: 0/8 health failed, nccl-tests completed, no kernel oops. perfbench: throughput -2%, p95 +4%.
ops-bot: posting to #incidents: summary: wave-0 clean, proceed to hold then wave-1 if no regressions in next 30m.
Maria: proceeding to hold. Wave-1 go/no-go at 13:50 UTC.
Priya: baseline artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-test-artifacts/driver-sweep/1855003210/baseline.tar.gz
Devon: oncall signoff readiness: yes.
Tanya: cost cap applied.
infra-bot: wave-1 scheduled: job_id=canary-1855-02, hosts=30, start=1855073400.
Maria: Thanks team — leaves here for now, ping me if anything weird.
